chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others, from Isa Shalan, who said:

I was sitting when Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) passed by, and with him was a goat. I said, 'O boy, what do you say about what your father does? He orders us with something then forbids us from it. He ordered us to befriend Abu al-Khattab, then he ordered us to curse him and disavow him.'

So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said, while he was still a boy: 'Indeed, Allah created a people for faith, from which it will not depart; and He created a people for disbelief, from which it will not depart; and He created a people in between those two, lending them faith. They are called the 'loaned ones' (al-mu'arun). When He wills, He strips it from them. And Abu al-Khattab was among those who were lent faith.'

He said: So I went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of what I had said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and what he had said to me. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'He is a spring of prophethood.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: A prominent companion of the Imams, known for his fluctuating relationship with them.
key_terms.أَعَارَهُ الْإِيمَانَ: Lent him faith, indicating a temporary bestowal rather than permanent creation.
key_terms.الزَّوَال: Departure or change, used here to describe the permanence of faith or disbelief for certain groups.
key_terms.الْمُعَارِينَ: The 'loaned ones', referring to people who are temporarily granted faith.
key_terms.نَبْعَةُ نُبُوَّةٍ: A spring/source of prophethood, a title denoting deep spiritual and prophetic knowledge.

ai.seo_question: What is the concept of temporary faith (Iman al-Mu'ar) in Shia theology regarding the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'al-Mu'aroon' (those with lent faith), using Abu al-Khattab as the primary example of individuals granted temporary belief that Allah may withdraw at His discretion, thereby explaining the Imam's shifting stance toward him. The young Musa ibn Ja'far’s concise explanation is validated by his father, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, who identifies it as a 'spring of prophethood' (neb'at nabuwah), highlighting the early manifestation of deep theological insight in the Imams. This concept underscores the distinction between innate faith and contingent divine grace, a key element in understanding the dynamics of the Imamate during the era of the Great Occultation's precursors.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary and someone else from Isa Shalqan who said,

‘I was seated and Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> passed by, and with him was a goat. I said, ‘O boy! What is your<sup>asws</sup> view of what your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> did, ordering us with something then forbidding us from it. He<sup>asws</sup> ordered us that we befriend Abu Al-Khattab, then he<sup>asws</sup> ordered us that we curse him and we should disavow from him?’

So Abu Al-Hassanasws said, and heasws was a boy: ‘Allahazwj Created a people for the Emān, there being no decline for it, and Created a people for the Kufr (disbelief) there being no decline for it, and Created a people between that, Lending the Emān to him, named as the ‘temporary ones’. Whenever Heazwj so Desires, Heazwj Confiscates it from them, and Abu Al-Khattab was from the ones who was Lent the Emān’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> and informed him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of what I had said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> and what he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> had said to me. So Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> is a spring of the Prophet-hood’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and others from ‘Isa Shalqan who has said the following:

“Once I was sitting when abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) passed by and with him was a goat. I (the narrator) asked him, ‘O young man, do you know what your father does? He commands us to do something and then he prohibits us to do the same thing. He commanded us to be friends with abu al-Khattab and then he commanded us to condemn and disown him.’

Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) said, and he was only a young boy, ‘Allah has created a creature for belief that does not vanish. He has created a creature for disbelief that does not vanish. He has created a creature in between and has deposited belief in them and they are called people with transient belief. When He wills He removes belief from them and abu al-Khattab was one in whom belief was deposited temporarily.’

I (the narrator) then went in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and informed him of what I had said to abu al-Hassan and what abu al-Hassan (a.s.) had said to me. Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘He is one of the fountains from prophet-hood.’”
